questions.text: What is the order in which the middlewares are executed?
questions.reference_answer: From first to last and then from last to first

questions.text: What is the purpose of CommonMiddleware?
questions.reference_answer: Adds various HTTP headers for better security and caching

questions.text: What is the purpose of CsrfViewMiddleware?
questions.reference_answer: Validates the CSRF Token and its origin

questions.text: What is the purpose of SessionMiddleware?
questions.reference_answer: Adds the session to the request and adds the cookies to the response

questions.text: What is the purpose of SecurityMiddleware?
questions.reference_answer: Helps secure your application by adding security-related headers

questions.text: What is the best place to set up a custom middleware?

choices.text: In a middlewares.py file at the project root
In a middlewares.py file in the app folder
In a middlewares.py file in a folder called middlewares
In a middlewares.py file in the project folder where settings.py is located

questions.text: Why are middlewares in Django similar to decorators?

choices.text: Because both wrap additional functionality around a view or request/response cycle without modifying the original view code
Because both are used to define database models in Django
Because both are required to create URL patterns in Django
Because both replace the need for views in Django applications
